The proposed control technique is implemented in PSIM using a 10 kHz sampling rate. The results are then verified in an experimental setting using a TMS320F28335 Texas Instrument DSP-equipped single-phase inverter prototype. The single-phase inverter has outstanding performance in terms of both steady-state and dynamic response. Furthermore, the proposed control method effectively minimizes the total harmonic distortion.

articleTitle: Identifying Gender Bias in Online Crime News Indonesia Using Word Embedding
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: In the digital era, news portals have become a primary source of information for millions of individuals. This study investigated the potential influence of word choice and gender representation in news on the public's perception of gender, emphasizing its implications for gender equality and human rights. Research has shown that the language used in news reporting can reflect gender bias, highlighting the significance of analyzing gender representation in crime-related news. A word-embedding model was employed to identify and mitigate bias in word representation and ensure fairness in the data analysis. This study aims to enhance our understanding of gender representation in Indonesian crime-related news and to apply word-embedding techniques to identify biases in word representation. The results indicate a potential bias in word embeddings, emphasizing the importance of addressing and mitigating biases in language models to avoid reinforcing unfair stereotypes.

articleTitle: Design of a Windbelt Array for Supporting Isolated Lighting Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Renewable energies have been attracting human interest since the fossil fuel reserve has degraded. Furthermore, renewables are clean energy sources that help to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, which are blamed for global warming. As a kind of renewable energy, it is believed that wind energy is one of the oldest and most widely used sources of renewable energy. In converting wind energy to electric energy, wind turbines are needed, including windbelts. Windbelts are dedicated to harvesting energy from the wind on a microscale based on an aerolastic flutter phenomenon. In this paper, a windbelt array has been built to support isolated lighting equipment. The test results show that the windbelt array starts to work when the wind speed reaches 2.0 m/s, producing a voltage of 1.6 V. The maximum working voltage of 3.9 V is achieved at a wind speed of 2.9 m/s. This working voltage is sufficient to support lighting equipment while charging the batteries.

articleTitle: Implementation of Broadcasting System for the 32nd SEA Game Via Satellite and Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The number of available TV shows has greatly increased as a result of the quick development of satellite TV transmission technology. The issue for cable TV networks throughout the world is to increase program capacity by rising the quantity of programs being broadcast. This is the first time for Cambodia to host the best event of the 2023 Southeast Asian Games. Satellite and Optical communications are the major transmission methods for this wonderful event. The goal of this paper is to present the results and analysis relating to the impact of the 32<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> SEA Game TV broadcasting.

articleTitle: Structural Analysis of Thumb Mechanism Exoskeleton Design for Post-Stroke Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Stroke is the second cause of death and the third cause of disability in the world. Stroke is a disease caused by a clot in the artery that supplies blood to the brain (ischemia). Rehabilitation is a solution to restore the function of parts of the body that have been disturbed by a stroke. Therefore, exoskeleton robots for stroke therapy are one solution to provide good rehabilitation. The exoskeleton robot supports healthy human hand movements and considers the safety and comfort factors during rehabilitation. The exoskeleton in this research uses a cable and sheath transmission mechanism with a locally situated motor as a design mechanism that guarantees safety and comfort. The design strength can be determined using ANSYS static structural assistance software so that the maximum stress in links 1, 2, and 3 is known within safe limits with anthropometric loading. Apart from that, the static structural simulation results show that link 1 can withstand a maximum load of 20 N or more in the X-axis loading, a load of 15 N in the Y-axis loading, and a load of 15 N in the Y-axis loading, and a load of 10 N in the Z-axis loading. Link 2 can withstand a maximum load of 10 N in the X-axis load and 20 N or more in the Y-axis load. Meanwhile, link 3 can withstand a maximum load of 20 N in the X-axis load and below 10 N in the Y-axis load.

articleTitle: Vibration Analysis for Damage Classification of Finish Good Conveyor Machine Using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: An industry engaged in the production of beverage products utilizes a Conveyor Finish Good (CFG) machine to facilitate the transportation of packaged goods to the storage warehouse during the manufacturing process. However, the lack of a monitoring system has made it difficult for the technical team to determine the appropriate maintenance procedures. As rotating machinery, CFG machines naturally produce vibrations that are influenced by the alignment and balance of their components. By measuring the intensity of these vibrations, valuable information regarding shaft alignment and balance accuracy can be obtained. To address this issue, industry has implemented a predictive maintenance system for CFG machines that incorporates vibration monitoring. The collected vibration data is utilized to identify any damage occurring in the CFG machines, with each type of damage exhibiting distinct characteristics in the vibration spectrum. The vibration spectrum is analyzed using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to facilitate the identification of amplitude and frequency, providing detailed insights into the specific type of damage present in the CFG machines. In addition, this research employs Neural Network (NN) technology to classify the various types of CFG engine damage. Through 18 experiments, the optimal NN architecture was determined to consist of 10 neurons in the hidden layer, with 50 iterations resulting in an MSE value of 0.045. The developed system is capable of accurately classifying the type of CFG engine damage in four conditions: normal, unbalance, misalignment, and looseness, achieving a maximum accuracy rate of 100 percent.

articleTitle: Realtime of Hand Gesture Recognition for Telerobotics Controller Based Leap Motion Using Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: In the era of human-robot collaboration and the advancement of telerobotic systems, the research presented in this study explores the development of a real-time hand gesture recognition system for telerobotics control. Leveraging the potent Random Forest algorithm in tandem with the Leap Motion sensor, our investigation delves into the intricacies of enabling intuitive and precise remote control of robotic devices. The primary objective of this research is to establish a robust, responsive, and adaptable system capable of recognizing hand gestures in real time, thus facilitating enhanced human-robot interaction.The result of the study reveals that the Random Forest model, when employed for hand gesture recognition, attains remarkable accuracy and reliability, with an accuracy rate of 98.61%, a recall of 98.60%, precision at 98.31%, and an F1-Score of 98.22%. Comparative assessments with alternative methods, including Random Trees, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Naive Bayes, demonstrate the superior performance of the Random Forest algorithm in this context.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of Financial Management Applications on Student’s Financial Awareness and Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The surge of electronic wallets (e-wallets) has profoundly reshaped how individuals, especially the younger demographic, manage their finances. This article explores the substantial impact of e-wallets on undergraduate students' financial management practices. To conduct this exploration, we utilize a comprehensive research methodology. Our primary approach involves bibliometric analysis, examining a diverse set of academic journals dedicated to e-wallets and their effects on undergraduate students. Data collection is facilitated by VOSViewer, a robust data visualization tool, complemented by co-authorship analysis and text mining techniques. The outcomes of these analyses are conveyed through bibliometric visualization maps, offering a graphical representation of the evolving trends and key contributors in this research domain. These maps provide insights into the intricate relationship between e-wallet adoption and shifts in the financial behaviors of undergraduate students. In essence, this research illuminates the transformative role of e-wallets in reshaping financial behaviors among undergraduates, contributing significantly to the understanding of this technological advancement in the realm of higher education.

articleTitle: Examining the Online Food Delivery Problem on Starlike Graphs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: When given incomplete information, an algorithm trying to solve a problem needs to resort to a heuristic to guide the choices in what is hopefully the right direction. This paper examined heuristics for an online scheduling problem known as the Online Food Delivery Problem (OFDP) over a larger context, expanding from the previously-studied star graphs to starlike graphs. Three heuristics were analyzed experimentally using randomly generated test cases for how well they do over the maximum flow time metric compared against an offline brute force algorithm. In order to simplify selection of requests for trips, two points were made that exploit the structure of starlike graphs to reduce the number of possibilities that need to be considered. Of the three heuristics, two of them, lowest anticipation time and highest flow time, performed better than the third (lowest flow time), with lower average competitive ratios and loose probable upper bounds of 6 for lowest anticipation and 5 for highest flow, compared to a probable upper bound of 7 for lowest flow. This paper also concurrently analyzed no-wait brute force, which is forced to set up a trip as soon as possible, similar to the three heuristics, but is otherwise offline, allowing access to full information. Its competitive ratios, both average and maximum, were lower than that of the heuristics, as expected. Also, its probable upper bound is likely 3, which aligns with the previous study on this problem over star graphs.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Approach for Data Integration on Tire Stacking Machine Through Real-Time Industrial Machine Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The utilization of real-time industrial machinery condition monitoring systems has emerged as an important component in improving operational efficiency, reliability, and equipment life. In specific industrial sectors, manual methods of data storage and retrieval are still used, leading to inefficiencies in data presentation. Widespread problems in these industries arise due to the absence of real-time data access. This research centers on a cost-effective approach to designing and implementing a real-time monitoring system for tire stacking machines. This paper introduces a real-time monitoring system on a tire stacking machine using Node-RED, equipped with integrated storage of stacking data, machine breakdown information, and process cycle time in a web dashboard powered by Grafana. The system can be accessed locally or via an industrial intranet network.

articleTitle: Improvement Heart Failure Prediction Using Binary Preprocessing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Heart disease is the deadliest disease, ranking first worldwide. There are various factors that contribute to the onset of heart failure, such as the nature of chest pain, blood pressure at rest, levels of cholesterol in the bloodstream, fasting blood sugar levels, results of resting electrocardiograms, attainment of maximum heart rate, angina triggered by exercise, oldpeak value, and the incline of the ST segment during peak exercise. Many research studies have been conducted using machine learning to obtain more accurate and effective predictions of heart failure. There are various machine learning algorithms that can be used for heart failure prediction. The algorithms used in this study are Gaussian Naive Bayes, SVM, KNN, Logistic Regression, Deep Learning, Random Forest Classifier, Decision Tree Classifier, and Extra Trees Classifier. Additionally, several sampling techniques were applied in this study, including Random Oversampling, Random Undersampling, Tomek Links, SMOTE and ENN for heart failure prediction. To obtain the best heart failure prediction, validated data on potential factors for heart failure occurrence is required. One platform that provides datasets on heart failure prediction is Kaggle, which has been widely utilized by researchers. In this study, the heart failure prediction dataset was processed using a comparison of several binary preprocessing techniques and machine learning algorithms to achieve high accuracy rates. From the conducted research, it was found that by preprocessing the data using Robust Scaler and applying the ENN Sampling with KNN algorithm, the highest accuracy rate of 92.61% was achieved on the heart failure prediction cases.

articleTitle: Visual-Based Battery Labelling Quality Checker System Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Having an auto labeling machine in the company is much faster and later determined by the company, but there are times when using an auto labeling machine results in incompatibility with the installation of battery labels. Apart from that, there are often claims from consumers that the label is not placed in the right place because the installation is done automatically. Based on this problem, we developed a machine that can detect the quality of label placement on batteries using machine vision. This machine vision technology is combined with the Convolutional Neural Network method. The system can detect label placement errors on batteries with a standard level of accuracy. The system can detect and classify three categories of battery label conditions with the average precision results for each class for no label batteries, rejected batteries and ok batteries respectively being 97.8%, 100% and 100%. The mean average precision (mAP) value produced by the detection model was 99.4%.

articleTitle: Spectrum Analyzer Using Software Defined Radio: A Case Study in Cambodia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Software-defined radio (SDR) is a crucial and contemporary technique in modern wireless communication. SDR is a type of radio that can tune to any frequency band supported by the hardware. It can implement various modulation and demodulation schemes, as well as different signal types and standards, all within the same device. Reconfigurable hardware and robust software make this possible. This paper offers an in-depth analysis of radio receivers based on SDR systems. SDR systems can implement primary devices such as a radio receiver, a radio transmitter, and a transceiver. The paper provides functions for both the transmitter and receiver. It also discusses the implementation of SDR devices using MATLAB, Simulink, and single-board computers. The emergence of low-cost SDR hardware with substantial functional capability has led to a reduction in the overall cost of SDR systems. Additionally, the paper compares different types of radio systems developed using SDR, along with an analysis of their performance. The program serves as a spectrum analyzer, enabling the visualization of the radio frequency spectrum for Frequency Modulated (FM) radio bands ranging from 88 to 108 MHz in Cambodia.

articleTitle: Exploration of an Electrical Energy Harvesting System Utilizing the Flow of Exhaust Emissions on a Motorcycle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the utilization of energy collecting devices within the exhaust ducts of vehicles. During the investigation, it is proposed to create an auxiliary structure that incorporates a turbine and is connected to a generator within the emission duct. When the exhaust gas flow encounters the propeller, it imparts rotational motion to the propeller, thereby driving the generator to generate electrical energy. The application commences by examining the characteristics of cross flow and Savonius turbine designs. Subsequently, the investigation focuses on the configuration of the supplementary structure and its orientation with respect to the flow. Additionally, the study explores the impact of altering the number of spins on the generator. Finally, experimental trials are conducted with additional bodies and propellers that are compatible with the vehicle. The design of this vehicle body aims to maintain pleasing appearances while ensuring the comfort of both drivers and passengers remains undisturbed. Based on the test findings, it has been observed that the augmentation of the body mass and the winding in the mechanism leads to a proportional boost to the generated electric voltage.

articleTitle: The Effect of Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) Implementation on Broiler Chicken Growth During Brooding Period
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: proper environmental management, such as temperature and humidity, plays a vital role in ensuring optimal growth and development during broiler chicken brooding period. However, this system has limitations in terms of long response times, leading to temperature and humidity Fluctuations. To overcome these issues, research has been conducted to test an alternative control system using Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC). This study aims to implement FLC in broiler chicken brooding cages and evaluate its influence on the growth performance of chickens. The FLC system utilizes temperature and humidity as inputs, while the outputs are PWM values to control fan speed and lighting levels. Two groups of broiler chickens were involved in this research, with One group subjected to the ON-OFF control system and the other group subjected to the FLC control system. Chicken growth was evaluated based on body weight, feed consumption, and feed conversion ratio (FCR). Data was collected daily throughout the brooding period and analyzed statistically to compare the two groups. The research results indicate that the implementation of Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) in broiler chicken brooding has the potential to improve feed efficiency, as evidenced by a lower Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR) of 1.034 for the FLC group compared to 1.121 for the ON-OFF control group. These findings suggest that utilizing Fuzzy Logic Controller in broiler chicken brooding management enhances growth performance, leading to improved feed efficiency and potentially better overall development.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of Four Omni-wheels Robot using PID and Pole Placement State Feedback Controller for Telepresence Robot Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: This research discusses an approach for controlling omni-wheel robots that will be used in telepresence robot applications. The first approach uses the pole placement method to control the motion of the inner loop, whereas the second employs the PID method to control the robot of the outer loop. The results demonstrate that the pole placement approach effectively controls the robot’s speed movement, whereas PID control can control the robot along the Y-axis. The system response in the simulations accurately followed the desired target trajectories. However, there is a performance delay observed in trajectory tracking along the X-axis, resulting in a 0.2m error after 1 s. Conversely, for trajectory tracking along the Y-axis, the actual performance successfully matches the provided reference, with an error of -0.04 within a 0.2-second duration. In the case of tracking the yaw angle with a target of 1 rad, the system consistently maintained excellent performance within a 2-second interval. Although response delays persist for the X-axis, Y-axis, and yaw angles, they continue to closely follow the desired targets. This research demonstrates that both control approaches can effectively control the motion of an omni-wheel robot according to the desired trajectories.

articleTitle: Design And Build of A Total Dissolved Solid (Tds) Control System to Maintain Water Quality in Koi Fish Ponds
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Koi fish (Cyprinus carpio) is one of the types of ornamental fish with high economic value that is highly sought after by many people every year. Despite having high economic value and a large number of enthusiasts, it turns out that Koi fish farming is not easy. Koi fish are prone to sensitivity to changes in water parameters, one of which is Total Dissolved Solids (TDS). The TDS content is influenced by organic matter such as fish waste, leftover feed, and ions in the water such as calcium, phosphate, nitrate, sodium, potassium, magnesium, bicarbonate, carbonate, and chloride. The acceptable TDS level tolerated by Koi fish is 500 ppm. If the TDS level exceeds 500 ppm, it is feared that it can affect the health and growth of Koi fish, such as damage to the gills, hindered growth rate, and susceptibility to diseases. The design of the TDS control system is done by measuring the TDS value in the water. If the TDS value exceeds the predetermined setpoint, the system automatically performs water replacement. This control system is also equipped with four additional sensors to monitor water parameters, including Dissolved Oxygen (DO) sensor, pH sensor, turbidity sensor, and temperature sensor for monitoring water quality. The validation process of these five sensors resulted in an error percentage of less than 5% with an accuracy of over 95%, which is considered competent for use in the created control system. The on/off control system has successfully reduced the water TDS from the highest recorded value of 534 ppm to 369 ppm when the control system has completed its operation.

articleTitle: Design of Portable Automatic Clothes Dryer with Fuzzy Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: This research presents an innovative solution to tackle the impacts of erratic weather changes and high rainfall on daily activities, particularly the time-consuming clothes drying process in Indonesia. The proposed approach involves the design and development of an automatic portable clothes dryer cupboard, integrating a fuzzy logic controller method, heating lamp, and exhaust fan to optimize clothes drying efficiency. As an essential component, the DHT22 sensor accurately measures humidity and temperature, providing vital input data for the control system. The control mechanism is implemented using an ESP32 microcontroller, employing fuzzy logic based on the Mamdani method to intelligently manage humidity and temperature levels for optimal drying results. Furthermore, the inclusion of an internet-based monitoring system, utilizing the Thingspeak platform, allows users to conveniently track the drying progress on their smartphones, enhancing user convenience and control. By minimizing drying time and maximizing space efficiency, this design addresses the challenges faced in densely populated urban areas where suitable areas for drying clothes are limited, often leading to aesthetic disturbances in housing arrangements. Ultimately, this automatic portable clothes dryer offers a practical and user-friendly solution, significantly improving the daily living conditions and comfort of individuals residing in regions prone to erratic weather patterns, contributing to a more sustainable and efficient approach to clothes drying.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Dual GPS for Heading Determination as a Compass Replacement in Unmanned Vehicles to Mitigate Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the experiment involving the use of two GPS devices as a compass replacement to determine heading direction. While heading direction can be easily determined using a compass sensor, there are scenarios where compasses may fail, especially in locations with strong magnetic fields. The primary concern addressed in this paper is the effectiveness of the dual GPS method as a compass sensor replacement and the determination of the optimal distance between the two GPS devices to maintain an acceptable heading error. Although heading direction can also be determined using a single GPS by calculating the movement from the current location to the previous one, this approach requires the GPS location to change, making it unsuitable for stationary autonomous vehicles. In our experiments, we placed two GPS devices at varying distances and calculated the heading direction based on the differences in their locations. The results of our testing revealed heading errors of 9°, 46.7°, 55.7°, 70.3°, 83.2°, 90.8°, and 161.6° for distances of 10m, 8m, 6m, 5m, 3m, 1m, and 0.4m, respectively. Based on our experiments, we determined that the minimum acceptable distance between the two GPS devices is 10m for reliable heading direction estimation.

articleTitle: Linked Open Legal Data Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Based on Regulation of the President of the Republic of Indonesia Number 33 of 2012, Indonesia legislation data can be accessed at the Jaringan Dokumentasi dan Informasi Hukum Nasional (JDIHN) which is located at https://jdihn.go.id/. However, all those documents are in PDF format, which are not machine-readable as open data. Hence, it is difficult to analyze data and re-use the data for other applications. Therefore, the research implements Linked Open Data (LOD) principles for publishing and consuming Indonesia legal data. We use https://schema.org/Legislation as the base vocabulary. In this work, we use Electronic Information and Transactions Law 2008 as an example of legal documents. The legal documents are converted to 1116 triples. In the final step, we give a showcase how to access the data by using SPARQL queries.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analyses for Assessing Renewable Energy Integration Aspects in Rural Areas of South Asia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive techno-economic analysis of hybrid renewable energy systems tailored for the specific contexts of San Kan, Myanmar, and Ratai Purwa, India. The focus is on integrating multiple renewable energy sources, optimizing system configurations, and assessing the economic viability to provide sustainable and reliable energy solutions for these regions. The analysis considers solar and wind energy resources and storage technologies to design efficient hybrid systems that meet the energy demand while minimizing costs (LCOE for San-Kan is $0.056 and for Ratai-Purwa is $0.061) and environmental impacts (Renewable Fraction of 98.2% for Ratai Purwa and 97% for San-Kan). The results emphasize the potential of hybrid renewable systems in contributing to energy sustainability and supporting socio-economic development in both regions.

articleTitle: Fake News Detection Using Sentiment Analysis Approach in Indonesian Language
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: In today’s digital age, information spreads rapidly. It makes news and any other information sources easily accessible and shareable. However, this convenience also comes with the risk of encountering false as well as fake information. This research aims to develop a system for detecting fake news using sentiment analysis approach. While earlier studies successfully used the VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and Sentiment Reasoner) method for English and achieving a noteworthy 78% accuracy with Random Forest, our focus is on designing a fake news detection system based on sentiment analysis for the Indonesian language. We extract extreme sentiment scores from news headlines and employ Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Naive Bayes for classification. Results from our experiment show Random Forest yields promising results, averaging 62% accuracy and peaking at 66%. This is a positive step in Indonesian fake news identification through sentiment analysis. Moving ahead, improving this system could greatly combat the spread of fake news. Future efforts may refine sentiment analysis, explore advanced ML techniques, and adapt to emerging news trends. Developing a strong fake news detection system via sentiment analysis contributes to promoting accurate information in our connected world.

articleTitle: Enhancing Hate Speech Detection for Social Media Moderation: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: In our ever-advancing technological age, a pressing concern emerges the challenge of preserving freedom of expression while combatting hate speech. Hate speech, in simple terms, involves hurtful messages directed at specific groups based on attributes like race, gender, and religion. Social media platforms have sought to curb hate speech through user reporting and automated content scrutiny, but their effectiveness is under scrutiny.To improve hate speech detection, we explore several machine learning algorithms, such as Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Decision Trees, and Gradient Boosting. By tweaking these algorithms and comparing their performance across metrics like AUC, CA, F1 score, Precision, and Recall, we aim to identify the best approach. Furthermore, our study reviews the current state of hate speech detection, presents the methodology used, and discusses implications for social media moderation.Our results show Random Forest as the top performer, but challenges remain. Future research may involve advanced classifiers, algorithm hybridization, and deep learning to enhance model performance in addressing the intricate landscape of online hate speech.

articleTitle: Prediction of Stock Trend Using Random Forest Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Stocks are financial investment instruments used by investors to generate a profit. Depending on the prevailing trend, investors typically profit from fluctuating stock price movements. Researchers in the field of artificial intelligence and investors are interested in this because the development of technology can assist investors in making decisions. One of the artificial intelligences utilized in this study is machine learning employing the Random Forest method to forecast stock market trends. Random Forest was selected because the ensemble method algorithm is particularly well-suited for use with data containing numerous features. It's just that this machine learning approach is not optimal because it requires adjustments based on the prediction target and has poor accuracy. Consequently, this study optimizes Random Forest by utilizing Random Search to obtain the optimal parameters for the classification model. In order to reduce noise in the data, Exponential Smoothing is applied to the features that will be utilized. Using the Random Forest method, this Research predicts stock price trends from transactional data. The dataset consists of historical stock transactions obtained from tradingview for 10 IDX stock issuers from several stock indices that are deemed to represent several areas of the company's industrial sector. The transaction data period is from November 2016 to November 2021, with a total of 1200 days of transaction data per issuer. This research includes the steps of data collection, data preprocessing, feature extraction, training mode, and model testing. Multiple methods, including F1-score, accuracy, precision, and recall, will be employed to evaluate the constructed model. The constructed model is compared to a random forest model in which the default parameters are used and the data is not smoothed. Based on the results of the comparison test, the optimized model has an average evaluation value that is 14.89% higher than the default random forest model.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Rain Detector Using An Electroda Probe On A Tipping Bucket Rain Gauge
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: A tropical country such as Indonesia experiences higher rainfall than other countries. Indonesia's BMKG, which monitors meteorology, climate, air quality, and geophysics, measures rainfall. They are currently being placed at certain points in Indonesia using manual tipping buckets. The problem with this tool is the inability to send data in real time. Our research involves creating a microcontroller-based rain detection tool that is connected to a long-distance communication system (LORA). As a result, the sensor data will automatically be sent to the server. Test results show that this tool can detect rainfall with 99 percent accuracy, which is almost as good as existing tools, and can transmit rainfall data over almost a kilometer distance in 699 ms.

articleTitle: The Implementation of A* Algorithm for Global Path Planning in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Path planning is utilized to design trajectory planning systems for autonomous vehicles. The A* algorithm has been proven successful in creating optimal, efficient, and safe navigation paths for autonomous vehicles. The resulting vehicle navigation path is an optimal trajectory considers heuristic values. The parameters employed in this research include the heuristic value, G-value (current cost), F-value (total estimated cost), Openlist, and Closelist. An average total estimated cost value of 2475 was obtained, with an average distance traveled over 10 seconds amounting to 139 meters. The results indicate that calculating lateral position from the path planning using the A* algorithm is reliable.

articleTitle: Identification System of Development and Growth of Cow, Goat for Increasing Investor Trust
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The problem experienced by cattle and goat breeder partners is that it is difficult to identify and monitor the growth of their livestock. Because the facilities on the farm are inadequate. So that it has an impact on investor confidence to carry out cooperation and management of livestock. The design of the livestock identification monitoring system that is carried is in the form of a qr code that will be worn around the neck of the livestock which will be scanned through the Android-based Livestock Assistance application which can bring up the identity and database related to the livestock. Investors can monitor their livestock in real time which functions as a monitoring medium to determine the condition, development and growth of their livestock. The digital livestock weighing scale facility has also been integrated in the Livestock Assistance application, so breeders and investors only need to enter the animal's body length and width so that the animal's weight can be obtained. The validation process was carried out at PT Sedana Peternak Sentosa to ensure the accuracy of the formula used in the Livestock Assistance application with the results of conventional cattle and goat weight scales. From the validation of the data, the results of the analysis show that the average cattle weight is 180.4 cm in chest circumference, 135.6 cm in body length, 410.8 kg in actual body weight, 407.8 kg in the Cattle Assist application with a presentation deviation of 0.009 %. Meanwhile, in goats, the average chest circumference was 68 cm, body length was 54.6 cm, actual body weight was 31.6 kg, body weight in the Cattle Assist application was 25.9 kg with a presentation deviation of 0.025%. This system is equipped with a livestock dimension measuring instrument using the HCSR-04 ultrasonic sensor which has a deviation percentage of 0.11% compared to conventional scales.

articleTitle: Jitter Clock Effect Analysis on Modular Dual Active Bridge (MDAB) Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The modular converter topology of Dual Active Bridge (DAB) is designed to distribute voltage and current evenly among each submodule. This process requires fast and accurate computation for pulse-width modulation (PWM) and feedback signals. During implementation, signal processing on the microcontroller faces various disturbances, one of which is clock jitter. Clock jitter has a proven negative impact on the performance of controller systems. Output stability in controllers with a single submodule can be significantly affected by jitter. This effect could lead to more harmful disturbances if implemented in modular converter circuits. The purpose of this research is to analyze the effect of clock jitter on the modular DAB circuit. The test was conducted by implementing a jitter value within a specific range. This value was then tested on a modular DAB simulation comprising of two submodules and various switching frequency. Based on these results, it can be seen that jitter interference in one of the DAB submodules can affect system performance. The voltage and current ripple values of the DAB1 and jittered DAB2 modules both increase with higher values of jitter and switching frequencies. This increased ripple causes the load voltage and current to become unstable. Consequently, this instability will negatively affect the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison Study Between DC Shunt Motor No. 110 and Three-Phase Asynchronous Slip Ring Motor No. 520
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Electric motors come in various types, including AC and DC motors. Each type of electric motor exhibits different performance characteristics, which significantly impact their application. This study aims to examine the performances of the DC Shunt motor and the three-phase asynchronous motor with slip rings by calculating parameters such as power, torque, and efficiency under loaded conditions. These calculations serve as a reference for selecting the appropriate motor to drive a Bow Thruster. In the DC shunt motor experiments, a DC voltage of 220 V was utilized, while for the three-phase asynchronous motor with slip rings, an AC voltage of 380 V was used. The results showed that the DC shunt motor produced a maximum output power of 297 W with an input power of 354.4 W, achieving a torque of 1.045 Nm and an efficiency of 86% at a motor rotation speed of 2715 rpm. On the other hand, the three-phase asynchronous motor exhibited an output power of 296 W with an input power of 318 W, generating a torque of 1.041 Nm and an efficiency of 93% at a motor rotation speed of 2720 rpm. The analysis revealed a relationship between several parameters and the motor load's impact on efficiency. It was observed that the three-phase asynchronous motor with slip rings demonstrated the highest efficiency and torque under the same load. Therefore, for the selection of the thruster drive, the recommended choice is the three-phase asynchronous motor with slip rings due to its higher torque value and greater efficiency compared to the DC shunt motor under equivalent loads.

articleTitle: Integrated Control System for Salt Purification Equipment to Optimize the Processing of Krosok Salt into Industrial Salt Using the Recrystallization Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The salt purification tool in this research functions to remove impurities contained in wholesale salt such as calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), and sulfate (S04). The raw material for wholesale salt was obtained from the Ronggolawe Makmur Tuban Cooperative which contains impurities of Ca 0.781%, Mg 0.793%, SO4 0.011%, and NaCl 89.27. In addition, this salt purification tool implements a level-based volume control system to regulate the ratio of sodium carbonate (Na2CO3), sodium hydroxide (NaOH), barium chloride (BaCl2), saturated water (brine), and wholesale salt entering the mixing tank. The test results for the volume control system obtained a value of Ts = 10.83 s, Mp = 1 cm, Ess = 0.3%, and Tp = 35.5 s, while the temperature control system obtained a test parameter value of Ts = 20.33 s, Mp = 1.67 0C, and Ess = 1.72%

articleTitle: Telemonitoring For Photovoltaic Systems Using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The usage of renewable energy sources, such as Solar Power Plants is growing in response to the problems posed by climate change and rising energy demands. Real-time and precise monitoring of operating parameters is crucial for maximizing the effectiveness and dependability of Solar Power Plants. In this context, the use of IoT technology in photovoltaic parameter monitoring systems is an innovative solution. This system is made to measure, collect, and communicate vital data in real-time, including light intensity, temperature, humidity, wind speed, voltage, current, and power. This solar panel monitoring system research technique makes use of the Internet of Things (IoT), which can monitor two photovoltaic units linked in a single converter unit by using the ESP8266 as a data processor and transmitter. An LCD display may be used to see data from numerous linked sensors. The estimated MAPE for each sensor is 1.17% for the Voltage Sensor, 0.0485% for the current sensor, 0.028% for the temperature sensor, 0.226% for the humidity sensor, 0.00725% for the light intensity sensor, and 0.089% for the anemometer.

articleTitle: Study of Slug-fly Ash Solution on Cyclone and Water Film for Steam Power Plant Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The Multi-cyclone Steam Power Plant Holtekamp confronts issues with fly ash accumulation in its flue duct and the adhesion of wet fly ash to water film-coated walls, leading to obstructions in the flue gas pathway to the Induced Draft Fan (IDF) and subsequent damage to the water film wall and IDF. The Multi-cyclone system's inadequate performance is evident in uneven flue gas distribution and reduced efficiency, especially for particles under 10 microns. Short-term solutions involve Multi-cyclone modifications, with the closure of the center section in Multi-cyclone 4 offering the most promising efficiency increase of 48.2%, albeit with a higher pressure drop. For longer-term mitigation, three options are considered: Multi-cyclone modification, Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP) procurement, and Bag House Filter acquisition. Utilizing the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), scores of 55.4, 73.3, and 80.8 are assigned to these options, with the Bag House Filter emerging as the most effective choice. In conclusion, addressing the challenges faced by the Holtekamp Steam Power Plant requires immediate action. Both short and long-term measures have been explored, and based on the AHP evaluation, the implementation of a Bag House Filter is recommended to rectify the issues stemming from inadequate fly ash management.

articleTitle: Design of an Adaptive Cruise Control System using PID Control Method on Electric Vehicle Prototypes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The use of Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles is still dominant in Indonesia due to easy access to petroleum-based fuels, but it has adverse effects on the environment. Vehicles are not only used for intra-city travel but also for long distances, increasing the risk of accidents as drivers may lose focus due to fatigue. To address this issue, environmentally friendly vehicles such as electric vehicles equipped with safety features to assist drivers are required. One such feature is Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), which helps drivers reduce speed and stop the vehicle when approaching other vehicles to avoid collisions. This research focuses on implementing LiDAR sensors to detect the distance between vehicles in the Adaptive Cruise Control system using PID control method as an additional feature in an electric vehicle prototype. The ACC system uses an algorithm that automatically performs vehicle speed adjustment based on the distance detected by the sensors. The ACC system will work based on the given input speed and adjust the safe distance as well as the minimum distance from the given input speed. The TFMini-Plus LiDAR sensor is used, and the tests show that this sensor has a high accuracy of 98.43%, with an error value of 1.57%. The performance testing of the ACC system shows that it functions according to the specified algorithm. The system is also able to respond well to new objects, with an average rise time of less than 2 seconds, overshoot less than 3%, and settling time less than 12 seconds. However, there are several faults in the encoder's readings of speed changes, leading to suboptimal analysis of the system's response.

articleTitle: Optimal Prediction of Electrical Energy Harvesting in Electronic Regenerative Shock Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to determine the best combination and generation of electrical energy from an electromagnetic regenerative shock absorber. The Taguchi approach predicts the optimal dimension between the number of coils, wire diameter, and air gap. Using the design of experiment L9 and plot effect, it was discovered that a combination of 2000 coils with a wire diameter of 0.4 and an air gap of 6 mm may generate the most electrical energy. It was then created and empirically measured based on these findings. As a result, there is a 5% difference between prediction and experimental measurement.

articleTitle: Basic Process Control System (BPCS) Design For Level Of Recirculating Water Tank Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The tank process plant is an essential part of the industry. It is evident that many industries utilize tank process plants, such as the system control level in the oil and gas industry. Over time, various issues have arisen with the system control level, such as slow dynamic responses to changing conditions. Water Level Control is one of the many systems present in the industrial world. By using this system, there is no need to worry about water overload or lack of water. The Basic Process Control System (BPCS) in the water level tank serves to control the water level in the plant. The plant's water level tank employs a closed-loop control system that utilizes a submersible level sensor and a PLC controller. The results of the dynamic response characteristics analysis with the values of maximum overshoot, settling time, and steady-state error are as follows: The maximum overshoot is 14.29%, the settling time is 578 seconds, and the steady-state error is 2.86%.

articleTitle: Remote Laboratory Using Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine as Distance Learning Support
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Remote laboratory is a system that allows users to access and control laboratory equipment via the internet remotely. Time and place limitations of the laboratory can be overcome by using a remote laboratory. The remote laboratory will use a horizontal axis wind turbine simulator. Remote laboratory system will use the Arduino Mega 2560 as the master and ESP32 as the slave which aims to transmit data on the website. Horizontal axis wind turbine functions as a simulator to produce the voltage and current generated by the generator. The wind source is obtained from a variation of 10 dimmer speed modes on the fan. The dimmer will be connected to the microcontroller so that the fan speed mode can be remoted via the website. The wind generated by the fan will rotate the turbine blades. The rotational speed per minute (rpm) of the turbine blades will be measured by the TCRT5000 sensor. So that there are 3 variables that will be measured using the sensor, namely voltage and current using INA219 and RPM using the TCRT5000. The results of INA219 and TCRT5000 readings will be displayed on a monitoring website which will be designed to support the distance learning process. INA219 sensor validation results obtained an error value of 1.51% and an accuracy of 98.49% for voltage and an error value of 3.37% and an accuracy of 96.63%. TCRT5000 sensor validation results obtained an error value of 2.08% and an accuracy of 97.92%. The system test results found that the blade 3 wind turbine cannot rotate at speed level modes 1 and 2. The blade 5 wind turbine is able to rotate at all speed level modes. The output of the blade 5 wind turbine has a higher voltage, current and RPM value when compared to the blade 3 wind turbine.

articleTitle: Development of Bemisia Tabaci Pest Trap Technology Based on Centralized PLTS (Off-Grid) as an Energy Source in One Hectare Edamame Agricultural Land
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Various methods have been employed to reduce and even eradicate the population of the edamame bean pest Bemisia Tabaci. Conventional methods, compared with other studies, have been used to increase edamame harvesting efficiency. In addition, technological innovation is required to create effective pest and insect control, one of which is a device that traps pests with a system of lights that can reach agricultural areas. Therefore, Bemisia Tabaci pest trapping technology is developed based on centralized (off-grid) PLTS as an energy source on edamame farmland. With an off-grid solar-focused power supply, this energy is stored in batteries that previously passed through the solar charge controller. Battery electricity will be used to activate 560–590 nm LEDs on each pest trap for 12 hours in a day. The total number of LEDs required to trap the Bemisia Tabaci insect is 13 traps; each trap is connected in series with 3 3.2 V LEDs, which will then be installed in parallel and glued. The energy produced by the solar panels is 345,768Wh, and the energy from the use of insect traps is 229,368Wh. Thus, the equilibrium energy in the pest trap system with concentrated PLTS is 116.4 Wh. The trap can last six days when using a 100-Ah battery. Pest traps can operate at night and trap up to 583 different types of insects in one night. The range of the pest traps reaches 15 meters per trap, and the overall range reaches 1 hectare of agricultural area.

articleTitle: Forecasting occupancy rate using neural network at Hotel R
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The hotel occupancy is an important factor to determine various policies in the hotel business. By hotel occupancy, hotel management creating targets in each department, determining hotel room prices, and stock management in F&B (Food and Beverage) and minor operating departments. In this study, occupancy rate forecasting was carried out for Hotel R using the neural network method. The dataset used in this study is room availability, room sold out, and available occupancy percentage at Hotel R from April 2018 to June 2023. The simulation was carried out by dividing the data into training data and testing data with a ratio of 60:40, 70:30, 80:20, and 90:10. Making neural network models is done using one hidden layer and two hidden layers. The forecasting results that have been carried out using a neural network with one hidden layer of optimal results were obtained for a 90%:10% data split with an RMSE of 0.009, while using a neural network with two hidden layers the optimal results were obtained for a 90%:10% data split with an RMSE of 0.016 (a difference of 0.007). The results of this study can be used by Hotel R in determining hotel policies in the future.

articleTitle: Design of Efficient Orienting Machinery System for Oil Bottle Position Selection Line with Fuzzy Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: In the oil filling production process, there are obstacles at the oil bottle position orientation selection stage, namely the position of the oil bottle which is still upside down or dropped. The cause of the obstacle is when detecting the orientation of the bottle with a tilted or dropped position, and also the unstable speed of the conveyor. These problems can affect the next production process, resulting in maintenance on the machine and production targets not being achieved. In solving this problem, an oil bottle position orientation detection is built with fuzzy logic control, the detection uses a combination of 3 infrared sensors. The placement of the three infrared sensors adjusts the shape of the bottle in order to detect the orientation of the bottle position, fuzzy logic control is obtained through the voltage output of the three sensors combined so that it can classify the orientation of the bottle position whether upside down, down, or in the same direction. If the orientation of the bottle position is detected to be upside down, it will move the stepper motor as a bottle orienting, and if the orientation of the bottle position is detected to have fallen, it will move the servo motor as a bottle sorter. Designing a system with fuzzy logic control can reduce the presence of inverted or dropped bottle positions, and also the tilted bottle position does not affect the detection of bottle position orientation. Assuming the entry of the bottle is intentionally upside down and falling, the orienting system can achieve 42% success and the sorting system can achieve 90% success, therefore the system can reduce the occurrence of maintenance caused by the position of the bottle upside down or falling.

articleTitle: Study of Traction Characteristics of a Low Multi-Purpose Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Vehicle traction performance is the vehicle's ability to move against the drag force that exists when the vehicle is operating. The power of the vehicle engine influences the capability of the vehicle, the choice of transmission level and ratio, and the type of transmission used so that sufficient driving force is required to overcome the drag force that occurs in the vehicle. This paper discusses the study of the traction characteristics of low multi-purpose vehicles. The study was carried out by calculating aerodynamic force, rolling resistance, and drag force due to grade angle at various velocities and gradeability to determine the total drag force. The study continued by calculating each gear transmission's driving force, net driving force, and maximum vehicle speed. The results show that the aerodynamic force has the lowest drag force, and the drag force due to the incline angle produces the highest drag force among the three drag forces that occur in the vehicle. Vehicles with 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> gear transmission can move up to 50% gradeability, followed by 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>, 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>, and 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> gears. Vehicles can drive well using 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> gear transmissions on flat roads.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation Effect of the addition of palm fronds on the burning of coal-fired boilers tangentially
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Biomass co-firing is an appropriate and cheap solution for achieving renewable energy targets towards net zero emissions because it can reduce the potential environmental impacts associated with burning fossil fuels. CFD simulations were carried out by adding palm frond biomass with a ratio of 5% and 95% LRC coal, which was injected into the boiler combustion furnace. The boiler operational parameters used in this simulation are a coal flow rate of 151.75 tons/hour and an airflow rate of 1184.33 tons/hour on the research subject PLTU Pacitan with a capacity of 315 Mw. The results show that adding palm frond biomass to burning coal changes calorific value, affecting the combustion process's high temperature. However, it has a good impact from the operational side of burning coal particles.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing of Multiple DGs in an Unbalanced Load Flow Using GOA Direct-ZBR and AGOA Direct-ZBR Methods to Determine The Lowest Active Power Loss Value
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: This paper proposes the Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA) and Adaptive GOA (AGOA) methods as optimization methods in placing multiple distribute generator (DGs) and sizing DGs in IEEE 15 bus unbalanced distribution systems. AGOA is a development of the GOA method by adding the LFD and Spiral Path methods in the population position update section. The unbalanced load flow (ULF) process in this paper uses the Direct-Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">BR</inf> method and has been verified with ETAP software results. The results of the unbalanced LF of the Direct-Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">BR</inf> method show accurate results after verification with ETAP. The GOA and AGOA methods also show the same optimal results by producing DG placement positions on bus 8 and bus 5 with capacities 1.5 MW and 2.0 MW respectively. After placing and sizing the DG, the active power loss value also improved by 34.78%.

articleTitle: Preliminary Studies for Cracking Sound Identification During Coffee Roasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: A coffee roasting plays an important role in determining the taste of coffee. The process consists of drying, browning, first crack, roast development, and second crack. The first crack is a beginning to form the characteristics of coffee beans. At this stage, a professional coffee roaster must ensure the spesific temperature and time, hence the beans are not getting burn. In manual coffee roasters, this causes inconsistency, because it really depends on the ability and experience of the coffee bean roaster. Therefore, in this study, we conducted a machine learning-based preliminary study to detect the cracking sound of coffee beans. The preliminary study was conducted by collecting videos of the roasting process from the internet. The videos are converted into audio format and separated between audio containing the sound of coffee beans cracking and audio that does not contain the sound of coffee beans cracking. The audios are then converted into an image format using the Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) method and modeled using convolutional neural network (CNN). From the 216 dataset files, we obtained an accuracy value of 89.7% with data lost during the testing process as much as 34.9% with 50 epochs of training and validation processes.

articleTitle: Understanding Human Face Shape via Inception-ResNet Neural Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: In recent years, computer vision has advanced facial recognition applications across diverse domains, from security systems to augmented reality. Among the fundamental attributes of a face, shape plays a crucial role in distinguishing individuals and understanding their unique identities. This paper introduces an innovative approach to comprehending human face shape through the cutting-edge Inception-ResNet neural network architecture, which combines Inception with residual connections. The approach harnesses the rich discriminative features learned by this architecture to boost face shape recognition accuracy and robustness. Extensive experiments demonstrate the remarkable performance of the approach, surpassing traditional methods and prior deep learning models. Furthermore, to provide a holistic perspective on the individual contributions of various modules within our approach, we present a detailed ablation study.

articleTitle: A Novel PH and TDS Monitoring System in Drinking Water
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: One of the parameter requirements for drinking water quality is pH and TDS (Total Dissolved Solid) of water. A good pH value with a value of 6.5-8.5 and a TDS (Total Dissolved Solid) value of <500 ppm according to the Regulation of the Minister of Health of the Republic of Indonesia No.492. The purpose of this final project is to make a prototype monitoring system with parameters of pH and TDS (Total Dissolved Solid) gallons of drinking water to provide information about the quality of gallons of drinking water. The final project method used is hardware design, hardware manufacture and is equipped with two sensors, namely a pH 201 C sensor and a TDS SEN0244 sensor. And the results of testing the pH 201 C sensor with an average error value of 3,367% so that it has an accuracy rate of 96,63%. Meanwhile, the TDS SEN0244 sensor has an average accuracy rate of 99,10 % and an error value of 0,90%. The results of testing the gallon drinking water monitoring system with a pH sensor value have an average error of 1,881% and an accuracy of 98,119% while the TDS sensor value has an average error of 0,7851% and an accuracy of 99,2148%.

articleTitle: Effects of Exposure Parameters on The RGB Channels of Clean and Polluted Insulators Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Flashover due to contamination is still an important discussion in efforts to increase the reliability of medium, high, and extra high voltage systems. The imaging technology offers several advantages in assessing the insulator condition. The camera settings play a very vital role as it directly determines the output image. But this aspect has not been investigated in more detail. This study exhibited the effect of exposure parameters on the image of clean and fan-shaped polluted insulators. The exposure parameters including ISO, shutter speed, and aperture were varied. In qualitative analysis, the output image from the visible light camera was observed visually. In quantitative analysis, the oval-shaped selection area was applied to the porcelain part of insulator. The RGB channels from the selection area were then separated. Furthermore, the curve shape and the curve highest peak were observed. The results revealed that the given variation in exposure parameter created visual impacts on the reflection level of non-porcelain objects and the sharpness level of pollutant distribution and density. The judgement of exposure parameter influence was more accurate based on the RGB channels. The changes in exposure parameter caused a shift in the curve position. There was a significant difference in the curve shape between clean and polluted insulators. Thus, the findings from this study could provide an overview regarding the optimal selection of exposure parameters for the insulator condition assessment.

articleTitle: Improved Artificial Neural Network Method for Predicting Temperature of Solar Panel Output Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Solar energy in Indonesia has great potential for advancing solar panel technology as an electrical energy source. Photovoltaic (solar panel) technology is known as a technology that utilizes solar energy and then converts it into electrical energy. There is a wide array of strategies available to articulate PV models. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the diagnosis methods used to model, control, forecast, diagnosis and classification detection and prediction. The application of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to renewable power systems has been developed many times before. Previous research has conducted studies on how to optimally size photovoltaic power systems and optimize installation costs. However, solar cell models have been developed to analyze the power characteristics of PV (photovoltaic) cell elements. Renewable power systems has been developed many times before. In this simulation of solar panel temperature prediction, measurements were taken including measurements of solar panel temperature, ambient temperature and irradiation as primary data. The training phase reveals a compelling regression plot, demonstrating an impressive R value of 0.8231. The minuscule error rate in the prediction system unequivocally affirms the exceptional quality of this ANN model.

articleTitle: Allocation of Reactive Power with Capacitor Bank Placement Considering the Use of Nonlinear Loads Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The bus voltage level on each bus in the distribution system (DS) is greatly influenced by the presence of reactive power (Q). Under voltage conditions can occur if the system lacks a Q value. Capacitor banks are the most effective solution in overcoming this problem. However, it can have a negative effect if the location and size to be placed is not optimal. The use of nonlinear loads can generate the spread of harmonic distortion and resonance can occur in the placement of capacitor banks. This research is the effect of optimizing reactive power allocation from the placement and size of capacitor banks considering the spread of harmonic distortion using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) which is validated on the ULP (subdistrict) Sungguminasa 165-bus DS based on MATLAB 2018b programming. Minimizing the %THDv and losses values is the objective function of the optimization process carried out in several case studies. Placing 4 capacitor units in case 4 with a total capacity of 1217 kVAr is able to reduce total losses by up to 3.14% or 12.24 kW, reduce the average %THDv value up to 0.566% and increase the average bus voltage level up to 0.254%.

articleTitle: Warehouse Management System Application using RFID Reader
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The warehouse at PT. Autonik Pack Machinery currently lacks a system to accurately check the actual stock levels, leading to confusion due to discrepancies in item naming. For instance, there are records of 10 "BEARING" pieces and 20 "bearing" pieces, which are actually the same item but are listed differently in the existing manual system. This mismatch between the recorded data and the actual stock in the warehouse can lead to unexpected stock shortages, and sometimes results in purchasing excess items even though there is still ample stock in the warehouse.To address this issue, a new warehouse management system is being developed. It will utilize a desktop application that tracks items as they are stocked in and out, and monitors current inventory, all with the assistance of RFID technology. The system, named Mywarehouse, will feature different access levels for various users such as administrators, accountants, management, and the electrical division. There is also an Android app that integrates with the desktop application, which will make it easier for employees to obtain the items they need and for accountants to track everything without waiting for updates from the administrators or having to physically check the warehouse.The new system has been tested to ensure its effectiveness. It has been rated at 97.9% for its functionality and 96.7% for its overall quality based on user feedback. Moreover, it has proven to be faster, taking approximately 7 seconds to process incoming stock, 5 seconds for outgoing stock, and around 3 hours to summarize all item data at once.

articleTitle: Long Short Term Memories for Microhydro Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The microhydro power plant harnesses river flow for renewable electricity production, contributing to the grid managed by the State Electricity Company (PLN). However, due to natural variables like rainfall, wind, and sunlight, accurate power forecasting is crucial for plant scheduling and daily operations. This study creates a forecasting model using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with historical data consist of power, water level, and rainfall data in which simulation employs optimally tuned parameters with comparison to Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. Results over day-ahead prediction shows that LSTM performance is shown as 79.05 and 0.12% for RMSE and MAPE, respectively. For ANN, the RMSE and MAPE are 46.60 and 0.12%, respectively. Meanwhile, results over week-ahead test period show LSTM with RMSE of 84.82 and MAPE of 0.01%, while ANN yields RMSE of 78.95 and MAPE of 0.01%. The LSTM model takes 52.6 seconds for 168-hour forecasting, compared to ANN's 0.27 seconds.

articleTitle: Minced Meat Classification using Digital Imaging System Coupled with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: Meat is widely recognized as a prevalent dietary choice due to its intricate nutritional profile, and its production constitutes a significant component of the global cattle industry. Due to the significant market demand for meat and the pursuit of maximizing profitability, meat products are often adulterated with additional ingredients. A diverse amount of meat can be effectively detected by the comparison model of machine learning. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the performance of low-cost imaging for classifying minced meat product. In this study, a variety of raw minced meat, including beef, lamb, and pork, was utilized. We investigated the feasibility of low-cost imaging system coupled with machine learning classifier such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, and AdaBoost Classifier. The findings indicate that the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) model exhibits superior performance, with an overall classification accuracy of 98.2%. The K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) model exhibits a notable level of precision and accuracy across all classes. Therefore, this study confirms that machine learning algorithm provide robust features for classifying minced meat from the image data.

articleTitle: DeksaCleannect: Conceptual Design of an IoT and AI Integrated Approach for Ocean Plastic Detection and Alerting System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The annual introduction of 8 million tons of plastic into oceans imperils marine ecosystems. Rivers, as conduits for terrestrial waste, contribute significantly to this marine contamination. To address this, we introduce "DeksaCleannect": a framework that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for real-time riverine plastic detection and alerting. DeksaCleannect, when strategically deployed, paves the way for proactive interventions, reducing the reliance on after-the-fact cleanups. Merging the robust data acquisition of IoT with AI's analytical capabilities, the system fosters swift community and governmental response. This paper explores DeksaCleannect's design, potential ramifications, and an integrated strategy that spans from in-situ water monitoring to aerial observations, targeting comprehensive plastic pollution mitigation.

articleTitle: Generator of Javanese Gamelan Musical Note Using 1D CNN Multi-Label Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: A song in Javanese gamelan has various patterns in playing according to the event it accompanies; variations of this pattern are usually found on the accompaniment instrument, not on the song's main melody. Nevertheless, in Javanese gamelan, the note of the written melody is only the main melody, so new musicians need complete note for all instruments; one of them is bonang barung. Therefore, this research produces an automatic music generator for bonang barung instrument as a musical accompaniment from the multiple input balungan note, rhythm, and song structure. This research is one of the topics in Music Generation, where the proposed method used Multi-label Classification using 1D CNN. Meanwhile, compared with gamelan experts, the results of this automatic generator from bonang barung note have almost the same results because the accuracy value of the proposed method 1D CNN is 87.62%.

articleTitle: Reliability Optimization of Compressed Air Systems in Nickel Smelter Industry based on Decision Making
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
abstract: The air plant is one of the important systems in the production process in the nickel smelter industry. The air plant consists of several compressors, distribution pipes, air sector systems, air dryers, separator tanks, and reservoirs. There are 13 centrifugal compressor units in the air plant which work with a total capacity of 49,000 CFM, while the demand is 35,000 CFM. The reliability of each compressor greatly influences the performance of the air plant, therefore it is necessary to determine the optimal number of compressors that can work on the air plant. The optimal number of compressors will result in higher energy efficiency so that production costs can be reduced. The purpose of this research is to produce maximum system reliability by determining the optimal number of compressors with a minimum air supply of 35,000 CFM. This research began with collecting maintenance data and piping and instrument diagrams, processing maintenance data, and creating an optimization model. There are three schemes as model variations used to obtain optimization values, when all compressors can work, when all compressors in section A3 are on standby, and when each section has one compressor on standby. The best scheme is shown when the system works with each section having one compressor on standby. This scheme has a system reliability of 0.655 when t is 4000 hours.

articleTitle: Harmonic Mitigation Using Passive Filters in 3-Phase Inverters to Improve Power Quality on Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Advanced Mechatronics, Intelligent Manufacture and Industrial Automation (ICAMIMIA)
